identity.name: Sodium malates
identity.chemical_class: Sodium salts of malic acid (hydroxy-dicarboxylic acid salts)

function.mechanism: Provides acidification/buffering and tartness through malate salts, supporting pH control and flavor balance.

adi.basis: No final EFSA numerical ADI was identified in the retrieved EFSA 2024 call-for-data re-evaluation material for E296/E350/E351/E352.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA published a 2024 call for technical/toxicological data for malic acid and salts, with scientific output requested by 31 Dec 2026, indicating re-evaluation is ongoing.

fda.notes: Direct Title 21 search for 'sodium malate' returned no hit; relevant human-food GRAS conditions are specified for malic acid in Part 184. Use is under GMP, excluding baby food, with category-specific maximum levels listed in 184.1069(d).

adi.basis: JECFA records for INS 350(i) and INS 350(ii) report ADI NOT SPECIFIED as part of the group ADI for malic acid and its sodium/potassium/calcium salts.

concerns.summary: JECFA group toxicology context states that for D(-)-malic acid and its salts, the ADI is not applicable to very young infants, indicating age/stereoisomer-specific caution.
Historical safety review data indicate irritation potential at certain cosmetic-use conditions, while systemic oral toxicity findings were generally low in reviewed animal data.

no_concern_confirmed: JECFA ADI for E350(i)/E350(ii): NOT SPECIFIED
No IARC monograph classification entry found for malic acid or sodium malate in the current IARC classification dataset
U.S. CFR Part 184 affirms GRAS status framework for listed direct food ingredients, including malic acid under 21 CFR 184.1069

populations: very young infants (D(-)-malic acid salt caveat)
adi_exceedance.notes: A numerical ADI is not set (JECFA: NOT SPECIFIED), so conventional percent-ADI exceedance calculations are not directly applicable; caution remains for very young infants in JECFA group context.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory evidence supports continued permitted use (JECFA ADI not specified; U.S. GRAS framework via 21 CFR 184.1069), with no IARC carcinogenic classification found. However, unresolved uncertainty remains due to EFSA re-evaluation in progress and JECFA's infant caveat for D(-)-malic acid salts.
key_factors: JECFA ADI NOT SPECIFIED for INS 350(i) and 350(ii)
21 CFR 184.1069 specifies GMP use conditions and excludes baby food
EFSA 2024 re-evaluation data call indicates pending contemporary EU scientific output
JECFA caveat for very young infants with D(-)-malic acid salts
